md_docs_2glyph-match-prototype(3) Library Functions Manual md_docs_2glyph-match-prototype(3)

NAME

md_docs_2glyph-match-prototype - Experimental glyph matching

--renderer=glyph enables a prototype foreground renderer in mirror, client, discovery, and MCP rendering. It fits an 8×8 pixel patch per terminal cell, averages that patch to 4×4, and compares its luminance and local structure with 95 printable ASCII glyph masks generated from DejaVu Sans Mono 2.37. The score balances normalized glyph density against per-sample deviations from the cell's mean. Foreground color uses the same nearest-neighbor sample as the current renderer. The default luminance renderer is unchanged.

The design was informed by Chafa, inspected at c897fce60cc4e947a254770ea1c2e320d58e7dce. Chafa uses 8×8 symbol coverage, selects candidates (or evaluates the whole set), estimates colors and scores the reconstructed cell. This prototype is an independent, smaller implementation; it does not copy Chafa code or glyph definitions. The generated font masks carry the license in lib/video/ascii/DEJAVU-LICENSE.

The atlas assumes DejaVu Sans Mono and a dark background. Other fonts, terminal color themes, and glyph rasterization can change the result. The prototype supports printable ASCII palettes. It falls back to luminance for Unicode palettes and in background and half-block modes. Optional --stabilize reduces frame-to-frame flicker in foreground, background, and half-block modes. The 8× sampling limits the viewport to 480×270 cells under the current image size limit; larger viewports fall back to the current renderer. It is a visual experiment, not a replacement for the default renderer.

Visual comparison

These are side-by-side captures from Windows x64 debug builds at 80×32 cells, truecolor, 8 fps. The emitted terminal frames were rasterized with Pillow and the same DejaVu font used for the atlas. The app-produced GIFs repeated their first image in this run, so they were not used for the comparisons. The left side uses the current renderer and the right side uses --renderer=glyph. The first three animations are roughly two seconds; their PNGs show frame 7. The website demo still shows frame 49. The two renderings of each test pattern were captured in separate runs and can differ slightly in animation phase. The FFmpeg clip is deterministic and was generated as shown below.

The comparisons cover test patterns 0 and 1, FFmpeg testsrc, and a silent 30-second excerpt of the website demo from 0:45 to 1:15. The source of the latter is web/www/public/assets/demo-video-white-knuckles.webm. Each side was captured separately at 8 fps and combined by frame index, so small differences in capture timing remain. The generated media is kept outside the repository.

The current renderer uses the standard 23-character ramp. The prototype searches 95 printable glyphs by default and scores their local shapes. An explicitly selected ASCII palette restricts the candidates; a Unicode palette currently uses luminance rendering. Both preserve the sampled foreground color.

Matching sometimes introduces directional glyphs at shape boundaries, while flat bands gain conspicuous repeated characters. The examples do not establish an overall quality improvement; font, image content, and motion need further evaluation. 

ffmpeg -f lavfi -i 'testsrc=duration=3:size=640x480:rate=8' -c:v mpeg4 -q:v 2 demo.mp4
ascii-chat mirror --test-pattern=0 --snapshot --snapshot-delay=2 --audio=false --fps=8 \


  --width=80 --height=32 --color-mode=truecolor --render-file=baseline.gif > pattern0-baseline.log 2>&1
ascii-chat mirror --test-pattern=0 --snapshot --snapshot-delay=2 --audio=false --fps=8 \


  --width=80 --height=32 --color-mode=truecolor --renderer=glyph --render-file=glyph.gif > pattern0-glyph.log 2>&1
# Repeat with --test-pattern=1 and --file=demo.mp4, naming the logs
# pattern1-{baseline,glyph}.log and testsrc-{baseline,glyph}.log.
python scripts/render_glyph_comparisons.py CAPTURE_DIR OUTPUT_DIR DejaVuSansMono.ttf
# Extract a 30-second action segment and capture it twice. Use the same options
# for both sides except --renderer=glyph.
ffmpeg -ss 45 -i web/www/public/assets/demo-video-white-knuckles.webm -t 30 \


  -an -c:v libx264 -crf 18 demo-action.mp4
ascii-chat --quiet --no-check-update mirror \


  --file=demo-action.mp4 \


  --snapshot --snapshot-delay=30 --audio=false --fps=8 --width=80 --height=32 \


  --color-mode=truecolor > baseline.log 2>&1
ascii-chat --quiet --no-check-update mirror \


  --file=demo-action.mp4 \


  --snapshot --snapshot-delay=30 --audio=false --fps=8 --width=80 --height=32 \


  --color-mode=truecolor --renderer=glyph > glyph.log 2>&1
python scripts/render_ansi_video.py baseline.log glyph.log website-demo.mp4 DejaVuSansMono.ttf

Renderer-only timing

On a Ryzen 7 5800X, WSL2 x86-64 Linux, Clang 14, Release -O3, AVX2 dispatch, 80×32 truecolor cells, three runs of 200 measured iterations after five warmups:

Renderer Mean time per frame across each run Current 0.016, 0.020, 0.015 ms Glyph match 2.293, 2.327, 2.332 ms

The test uses the first frame of the FFmpeg clip, cropped to the viewport and nearest-neighbor sampled to 640×256. The baseline takes one sample per cell; the matcher receives the 8×8 patch. Both calls allocate and emit text. Timings exclude image fitting/resizing, capture, encoding, terminal writes, and the rest of the application. The matching stage is roughly 145× slower using the median values in this small benchmark, though still below a 16.7 ms frame budget by itself. This is not an end-to-end throughput guarantee; concurrent load and other platforms can differ. 

ffmpeg -v error -i demo.mp4 -vf 'crop=240:480:200:0,scale=640:256:flags=neighbor' \


  -frames:v 1 -pix_fmt rgb24 -f rawvideo benchmark.rgb
cmake -S tests/simd -B /tmp/glyph-simd -G Ninja -DTEST_EMISSION=ON \


  -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build /tmp/glyph-simd --target emission-test glyph-benchmark
ctest --test-dir /tmp/glyph-simd -R simd-emission --output-on-failure
/tmp/glyph-simd/glyph-benchmark benchmark.rgb
